Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration. It is mathematically the sum of Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) and Residual Volume (RV). Since RV is a positive volume (1100 mL to 1200 mL), FRC is always greater than ERV.

Reason (R) is false: While FRC does include the Residual Volume (RV), RV is defined as the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration. It cannot be expelled from the lungs.

Therefore, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the process of breathing, which of the following events specifically causes an increase in the volume of the thoracic chamber in the dorso-ventral axis?
options: Contraction of the external intercostal muscles
Relaxation of the external intercostal muscles
Contraction of the internal intercostal muscles
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, inspiration is initiated by the contraction of the diaphragm, which increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis.

The contraction of external intercostal muscles lifts up the ribs and the sternum, causing an increase in the volume of the thoracic chamber in the dorso-ventral axis.

Relaxation of these muscles leads to a decrease in thoracic volume (normal expiration), while the contraction of internal intercostal muscles is involved in forced expiration.

Answer: Contraction of the external intercostal muscles

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) The respiratory rhythm centre is located in the pons region of the hindbrain.
(B) The enzyme carbonic anhydrase is completely absent in blood plasma.
(C) A sigmoid curve is obtained when percentage saturation of haemoglobin with $\text{O}_2$ is plotted against $\text{pO}_2$.
(D) Alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system.

How many of the above statements are incorrect?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because the respiratory rhythm centre is located in the medulla region of the hindbrain, whereas the pneumotaxic centre is located in the pons region.

Statement (B) is incorrect because while carbonic anhydrase is present in very high concentration in RBCs, minute quantities of the same are also present in the plasma.

Statement (C) is correct as the Oxygen Dissociation Curve is highly sigmoid.

Statement (D) is correct as the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system.

Therefore, exactly two statements are incorrect.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Under normal physiological conditions, what volume of carbon dioxide is delivered to the alveoli by every $100\text{ ml}$ of deoxygenated blood?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, every $100\text{ ml}$ of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately $4\text{ ml}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ to the alveoli.

The value $5\text{ ml}$ corresponds to the amount of $\text{O}_2$ delivered to the tissues by every $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood, while $20\text{ ml}$ is the approximate total carrying capacity of oxygen per $100\text{ ml}$ of blood.

Answer: $4\text{ ml}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: To expel the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) from the lungs, a person must perform a forcible expiration. Which of the following muscular events is required to achieve this?
options: Contraction of additional muscles in the abdomen
Relaxation of the diaphragm and external inter-costal muscles only
Contraction of the diaphragm and external inter-costal muscles
Relaxation of the abdominal muscles along with contraction of the diaphragm
questions.solution:
Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) is defined as the additional volume of air a person can expire by a forcible expiration.

Normal expiration is a passive process that occurs due to the relaxation of the diaphragm and external inter-costal muscles. However, to perform a forcible expiration and expel the ERV, active muscle contraction is required. Humans have the ability to increase the strength of expiration with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen.

Therefore, the contraction of abdominal muscles facilitates the forceful expulsion of the Expiratory Reserve Volume.

Answer: Contraction of additional muscles in the abdomen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Neural signals from the pneumotaxic centre can alter the respiratory rate.
Reason (R): The pneumotaxic centre can reduce the duration of inspiration by moderating the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the pneumotaxic centre is located in the pons region of the brain and moderates the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla.

Neural signals from the pneumotaxic centre reduce the duration of inspiration. By shortening the inspiratory phase, the overall respiratory rate is altered (increased).

Therefore, the assertion is a true statement, and the reason is also true and provides the correct physiological mechanism explaining how the pneumotaxic centre alters the respiratory rate.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During extreme environmental conditions such as summer sleep (aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation), frogs respire exclusively through their:
questions.solution:
Frogs undergo aestivation (summer sleep) and hibernation (winter sleep) to protect themselves from extreme heat and cold by burrowing deep into the mud.

During these dormant periods, pulmonary and buccal respiration cannot occur. The frogs rely entirely on cutaneous respiration, where gaseous exchange takes place exclusively through their moist skin.

Lungs and buccal cavity are used on land, while gills are present only in the larval (tadpole) stage.

Answer: skin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the option that correctly states the physiological description and the mathematical expression for Functional Residual Capacity (FRC).
options: Volume of air remaining in the lungs after a forced expiration; RV
Total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration; TV + ERV
Volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal expiration; TV + RV
Volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration; ERV + RV
questions.solution:
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is defined as the volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration. It is mathematically expressed as the sum of Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) and Residual Volume (RV).

Option 1 describes Residual Volume (RV).
Option 2 describes Expiratory Capacity (EC).
Option 3 provides an incorrect mathematical formula for FRC.

Answer: Volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration; ERV + RV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the sequence of human respiration, the diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues does not occur immediately after their diffusion across the alveolar membrane.

Reason (R): Transport of gases by the blood acts as an essential intermediate step to carry $\text{O}_2$ from the lungs to the systemic tissues and $\text{CO}_2$ from the tissues to the lungs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Respiration in humans involves a strict sequence of five steps. The first step is pulmonary ventilation, followed by the second step, which is the diffusion of gases across the alveolar membrane. The third step is the transport of gases by the blood. The fourth step is the diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues, and the final step is cellular respiration.

Assertion (A) is correct because the two distinct diffusion events (alveolar level and tissue level) are separated temporally and spatially by the transport phase. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact physiological explanation for this separation: blood must physically carry the gases between the respiratory surface (lungs) and the target sites (systemic tissues). Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Inspiratory Capacity(I) ERV + RV
(B) Expiratory Capacity(II) Total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration
(C) Functional Residual Capacity(III) TV + IRV
(D) Total Lung Capacity(IV) TV + ERV

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT:
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. It includes TV + IRV.
Expiratory Capacity (EC) is the total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration. It includes TV + ERV.
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration. It includes ERV + RV.
Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. It includes RV, ERV, TV, and IRV.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During strenuous exercise, skeletal muscles require an increased supply of oxygen. Which of the following local changes in the muscle tissue environment facilitate the increased release of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin?
options: Increase in $p\text{CO}_2$, increase in $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and increase in temperature
Decrease in $p\text{CO}_2$, decrease in $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and decrease in temperature
Increase in $p\text{CO}_2$, decrease in $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and decrease in temperature
Decrease in $p\text{CO}_2$, increase in $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and decrease in temperature
questions.solution:
During strenuous exercise, the metabolic rate of skeletal muscles increases significantly. This leads to a higher production of carbon dioxide (increasing $p\text{CO}_2$), an accumulation of metabolic acids like lactic acid and carbonic acid (increasing $\text{H}^+$ concentration or lowering pH), and the generation of more heat (increasing temperature).

According to the Bohr effect, an increase in $p\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}^+$ concentration, along with an increase in temperature, decreases the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen. This causes a right shift in the oxygen dissociation curve, facilitating the release of more oxygen to the active muscle tissues.

Answer: Increase in $p\text{CO}_2$, increase in $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and increase in temperature

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II regarding the mechanism of breathing.

Column IColumn II
A. Contraction of diaphragm1. Increases volume in dorso-ventral axis
B. Contraction of external intercostal muscles2. Increases volume in antero-posterior axis
C. Relaxation of diaphragm3. Inspiration
D. Intrapulmonary pressure less than atmospheric pressure4. Expiration

Choose the correct option from the following:
questions.solution:
According to the mechanism of breathing:

Contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis (A-2).

Contraction of the external intercostal muscles lifts up the ribs and sternum, causing an increase in the volume of the thoracic chamber in the dorso-ventral axis (B-1).

Relaxation of the diaphragm and intercostal muscles reduces the thoracic volume, leading to an increase in intrapulmonary pressure and causing expiration (C-4).

Inspiration occurs when the intrapulmonary pressure is less than the atmospheric pressure, creating a negative pressure in the lungs (D-3).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

Answer: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the correct name and the standard average value of the volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration in a healthy human.
questions.solution:
The volume of air that remains in the lungs after a normal expiration is called the Functional Residual Capacity (FRC).

It includes the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) and the Residual Volume (RV).

FRC = ERV + RV

According to standard physiological values in a healthy human:
ERV = $1000 - 1100$ mL
RV = $1100 - 1200$ mL

Therefore, FRC = $(1000 + 1100)$ to $(1100 + 1200)$ mL = $2100 - 2300$ mL.

Residual Volume ($1100 - 1200$ mL) is the air remaining after a forcible expiration. Expiratory Capacity ($1500 - 1600$ mL) is the total volume of air expired after a normal inspiration.

Answer: Functional Residual Capacity; $2100 - 2300$ mL

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the steps of respiration.

(A)Pulmonary ventilation(I)Use of $\mathrm{O}_2$ for catabolic reactions and release of $\mathrm{CO}_2$
(B)Alveolar diffusion(II)Atmospheric air is drawn in and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ rich air is released out
(C)Transport of gases(III)Movement of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ mediated by blood
(D)Cellular utilisation(IV)Exchange of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ across the respiratory membrane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the steps of respiration are:
1. Breathing or pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out (A matches with II).
2. Diffusion of gases ($\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$) across alveolar membrane (B matches with IV).
3. Transport of gases by the blood (C matches with III).
4. Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues.
5. Utilisation of $\mathrm{O}_2$ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ (D matches with I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following sets of conditions will decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, causing a right shift in the oxygen dissociation curve?
options: High $p\text{O}_2$, low $p\text{CO}_2$, less $\text{H}^+$ concentration, lower temperature
Low $p\text{O}_2$, low $p\text{CO}_2$, more $\text{H}^+$ concentration, higher temperature
Low $p\text{O}_2$, high $p\text{CO}_2$, less $\text{H}^+$ concentration, lower temperature
Low $p\text{O}_2$, high $p\text{CO}_2$, more $\text{H}^+$ concentration, higher temperature
questions.solution:
A right shift in the oxygen dissociation curve indicates a decreased affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, which promotes the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

These conditions are typically found in the tissues where oxygen is consumed and carbon dioxide is produced. The factors that favour this dissociation are low $p\text{O}_2$, high $p\text{CO}_2$, high $\text{H}^+$ concentration (lower pH), and higher temperature.

High $p\text{O}_2$, low $p\text{CO}_2$, less $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and lower temperature are conditions found in the alveoli that favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin (a left shift).

Answer: Low $p\text{O}_2$, high $p\text{CO}_2$, more $\text{H}^+$ concentration, higher temperature

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The human respiratory system consists of a conducting part and an exchange (respiratory) part. Which of the following major steps of respiration corresponds strictly to the primary physiological function of the exchange part?
options: Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ across the alveolar membrane
Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in
Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
Transport of respiratory gases by the blood
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the respiratory system is divided into a conducting part and an exchange part. The exchange part (alveoli and their ducts) is the site of actual diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ between blood and atmospheric air.

Therefore, the step 'Diffusion of gases ($\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$) across alveolar membrane' strictly represents the function of the exchange part.

Pulmonary ventilation involves both parts to move air in and out. Transport of gases is a function of the cardiovascular system, and diffusion between blood and tissues occurs at the systemic capillaries, not the respiratory exchange part.

Answer: Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ across the alveolar membrane

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
A healthy adult individual undergoes a pulmonary function test. The following respiratory values are recorded:

Total Lung Capacity (TLC) = $5800\text{ mL}$
Residual Volume (RV) = $1200\text{ mL}$
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) = $3500\text{ mL}$

Based on the given data, what is the value of the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) for this individual?
questions.solution:
Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. It is the sum of Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV), Tidal Volume (TV), Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), and Residual Volume (RV).

Since Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the sum of IRV and TV, the formula for TLC can be written as:
$\text{TLC} = \text{IC} + \text{ERV} + \text{RV}$

Given:
$\text{TLC} = 5800\text{ mL}$
$\text{IC} = 3500\text{ mL}$
$\text{RV} = 1200\text{ mL}$

Substituting the values:
$5800 = 3500 + \text{ERV} + 1200$
$5800 = 4700 + \text{ERV}$
$\text{ERV} = 5800 - 4700 = 1100\text{ mL}$

Calculating $\text{TLC} - \text{IC}$ alone gives the Functional Residual Capacity ($2300\text{ mL}$), and $\text{TLC} - \text{RV}$ gives the Vital Capacity ($4600\text{ mL}$).

Answer: $1100\text{ mL}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Inspiration can occur if the intra-pulmonary pressure is less than the atmospheric pressure.
Reason (R): Contraction of diaphragm and external intercostal muscles decreases the overall thoracic volume, creating a negative pressure in the lungs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is a correct statement. Inspiration occurs when the pressure within the lungs (intra-pulmonary pressure) is less than the atmospheric pressure, establishing a negative pressure gradient.

Reason (R) is an incorrect statement. The contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles increases, not decreases, the overall thoracic volume. This increase in thoracic volume leads to an increase in pulmonary volume, which in turn decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure below atmospheric pressure, causing air to rush into the lungs.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the following physiological events of inspiration in the correct chronological sequence:

(A) Increase in pulmonary volume
(B) Air moves into the lungs
(C) Contraction of diaphragm and external intercostal muscles
(D) Decrease in intra-pulmonary pressure
(E) Increase in the volume of thoracic chamber

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of events during inspiration is:

1. Inspiration is initiated by the contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles (C).
2. This contraction increases the overall volume of the thoracic chamber (E).
3. The increase in thoracic volume causes a similar increase in pulmonary volume (A), because the lungs are situated in the air-tight thoracic chamber.
4. An increase in pulmonary volume leads to a decrease in intra-pulmonary pressure to less than the atmospheric pressure (D).
5. This pressure gradient forces the air from outside to move into the lungs (B).

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is (C) → (E) → (A) → (D) → (B).

Answer: (C) → (E) → (A) → (D) → (B)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding respiratory organs in animals.

List-IList-II
(A) Flatworms(I) Moist cuticle
(B) Earthworms(II) Gills
(C) Insects(III) Simple diffusion over entire body surface
(D) Aquatic arthropods(IV) Tracheal tubes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Based on the breathing mechanisms described in NCERT:

(A) Flatworms (along with sponges and coelenterates) exchange $O_2$ with $CO_2$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. (A matches III)

(B) Earthworms use their moist cuticle for gas exchange. (B matches I)

(C) Insects have a network of tubes called tracheal tubes to transport atmospheric air within the body. (C matches IV)

(D) Aquatic arthropods (and molluscs) use special vascularised structures called gills. (D matches II)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(I) Every $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood can deliver around $5\text{ ml}$ of $\text{O}_2$ to the tissues under normal physiological conditions.
(II) High $\text{pO}_2$ and low $\text{pCO}_2$ in alveoli are favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
(III) A rise in $\text{H}^+$ concentration in the blood shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the left.
(IV) The binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is primarily related to the partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct as per NCERT; under normal physiological conditions, every $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood delivers around $5\text{ ml}$ of $\text{O}_2$ to the tissues.

Statement (II) is correct because in the alveoli, high $\text{pO}_2$, low $\text{pCO}_2$, lesser $\text{H}^+$ concentration and lower temperature are the factors that favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.

Statement (III) is incorrect because a rise in $\text{H}^+$ concentration (which means a decrease in pH) favours the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin, thereby shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the right.

Statement (IV) is incorrect because the binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is primarily related to the partial pressure of $\text{O}_2$. The partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$ can interfere with this binding, but it is not the primary factor.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms exchange O_2$ with CO_2$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.

Reason (R): Mechanisms of breathing vary among different groups of animals depending mainly on their habitats, but are independent of their levels of organisation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because lower invertebrates such as sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms lack complex respiratory organs and rely on simple diffusion over their entire body surface for the exchange of gases.

Reason (R) is incorrect because the mechanisms of breathing vary among different groups of animals depending mainly on both their habitats and their levels of organisation, not independent of the latter.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the systemic tissues, the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve shifts to the left.
Reason (R): High pC$O_2$, high H$^+$ concentration, and higher temperature in the tissues decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because in the systemic tissues, the conditions favour the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin, which corresponds to a shift of the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve to the right, not the left.

Reason (R) is correct. The systemic tissues are characterised by low pO_2$, high pCO_2$, high H$^+$ concentration (low pH), and higher temperature. These factors decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, facilitating its release (unloading) to the tissues.

Therefore, the Assertion is incorrect but the Reason is correct.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the sequence of respiration in humans, which physiological step acts as the chronological link between the exchange of gases occurring across the simple squamous epithelium of the alveoli and the exchange of gases occurring at the systemic capillaries?
options: Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
Transport of gases by the blood
questions.solution:
Respiration in humans occurs in a specific sequence of five steps.

The exchange of gases across the simple squamous epithelium of the alveoli represents the second step (alveolar diffusion).

The exchange of gases at the systemic capillaries represents the fourth step (diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues).

The physiological step that chronologically and functionally links these two events is the third step, which is the transport of gases by the blood.

Pulmonary ventilation is the first step (occurring before alveolar diffusion), and cellular respiration is the fifth step (occurring after tissue diffusion).

Answer: Transport of gases by the blood

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Earthworms exchange gases with their environment primarily through their _________.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, earthworms use their moist cuticle for the exchange of gases.

Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms exchange gases by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Insects have a network of tracheal tubes, while most aquatic arthropods and molluscs use gills.

Answer: moist cuticle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During normal expiration, air moves out of the lungs because intrapulmonary pressure becomes slightly higher than atmospheric pressure.
Reason (R): Relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles decreases the thoracic volume, which leads to an increase in intrapulmonary pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the movement of air into or out of the lungs is driven by pressure gradients. For expiration to occur, the pressure inside the lungs (intrapulmonary pressure) must be higher than the atmospheric pressure, forcing air outward.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the accurate physiological mechanism for this pressure change. Normal expiration is a passive process initiated by the relaxation of the primary inspiratory muscles (the diaphragm and external intercostals). This relaxation returns the diaphragm to its dome shape and the ribs to their normal position, thereby reducing the overall thoracic volume. According to Boyle's law, a decrease in volume leads to an increase in pressure. This raises the intrapulmonary pressure slightly above atmospheric pressure.

Therefore, Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the human respiratory system:
A. The conducting part transports atmospheric air to the alveoli and brings it to body temperature.
B. The conducting part extends from the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles.
C. All structures of the conducting part are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings.

Choose the correct option.
options: Statements A and B are correct
Statements A, B and C are correct
Statements A and C are correct
Statements B and C are correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitutes the conducting part. Thus, statement B is correct.

The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Thus, statement A is correct.

The trachea, primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings. The terminal bronchioles are part of the conducting zone but lack these cartilaginous rings. Therefore, not all structures of the conducting part are supported by them. Thus, statement C is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: Statements A and B are correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Total Lung Capacity (TLC) and Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) can be directly measured using a simple clinical spirometer.

Reason (R): A simple spirometer cannot measure the Residual Volume (RV), which is a necessary component of both TLC and FRC.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because a simple clinical spirometer can only measure the volume of air that can be breathed in and out. It cannot measure the air that remains in the lungs after forceful expiration.

Reason (R) is true. Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration, meaning it never enters the spirometer. Since Total Lung Capacity (TLC) and Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) both include RV in their composition (TLC = Vital Capacity + RV, and FRC = Expiratory Reserve Volume + RV), they cannot be measured directly by a simple spirometer.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding respiratory volumes and capacities:

Statement A : Total Lung Capacity (TLC) minus Residual Volume (RV) equals Vital Capacity (VC).
Statement B : Inspiratory Capacity (IC) includes the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV).
Statement C : The volume of air involved in breathing movements can be estimated by using a spirometer.
Statement D : Residual Volume (RV) can be directly measured using a standard spirometer.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration. TLC = Vital Capacity (VC) + Residual Volume (RV). Therefore, TLC $-$ RV = VC.

Statement B is incorrect: Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. It includes Tidal Volume (TV) and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV). It does not include ERV.

Statement C is correct: The volume of air involved in breathing movements can be estimated by using a spirometer, which helps in the clinical assessment of pulmonary functions.

Statement D is incorrect: Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration. Since this air cannot be exhaled, it cannot be directly measured using a standard spirometer.

Thus, exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
At the tissue site, high $\text{pCO}_2$ causes $\text{CO}_2$ to diffuse into the blood, where a specific enzyme rapidly catalyses its hydration. The resulting increase in $\text{H}^+$ concentration affects the oxygen dissociation curve.

Identify the enzyme, its primary location in the blood, and the direction in which the oxygen dissociation curve shifts as a result of this process.
options: Carbonic anhydrase, RBCs, Shift to the right
Carbonic anhydrase, RBCs, Shift to the left
Carbonic anhydrase, Plasma, Shift to the right
Carbonic anhydrase, Plasma, Shift to the left
questions.solution:
At the tissue level, high $\text{pCO}_2$ and low $\text{pO}_2$ favour the dissociation of oxygen from haemoglobin. $\text{CO}_2$ diffuses into the blood and forms carbonic acid, a reaction catalysed by the enzyme carbonic anhydrase. This enzyme is present in very high concentration in the RBCs (and only in minute quantities in the plasma). The formation of carbonic acid and its subsequent dissociation increases the $\text{H}^+$ concentration (lowers pH). High $\text{pCO}_2$ and high $\text{H}^+$ concentration are factors that shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the right, promoting the release of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

Answer: Carbonic anhydrase, RBCs, Shift to the right

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are the physiological steps involved in the elimination of carbon dioxide from the human body:
(A) Transport of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ by the blood.
(B) Release of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ by the cells resulting from catabolic reactions.
(C) Diffusion of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ across the alveolar membrane into the alveolar cavity.
(D) Diffusion of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ from the tissues into the blood.
(E) Pulmonary ventilation by which $\mathrm{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out.

Select the correct chronological sequence of these events, starting from the production of $\mathrm{CO}_2$:
questions.solution:
The elimination of carbon dioxide follows the reverse path of oxygen uptake.

The correct chronological sequence begins with the production of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ during cellular catabolism (B).

This $\mathrm{CO}_2$ then diffuses from the tissues into the bloodstream (D).

The blood transports the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ to the lungs (A).

At the lungs, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ diffuses across the alveolar membrane into the alveolar cavity (C).

Finally, pulmonary ventilation expels the $\mathrm{CO}_2$-rich alveolar air to the exterior (E).

Thus, the correct sequence is (B), (D), (A), (C), (E).

Answer: (B), (D), (A), (C), (E)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A person forcefully exhales air to blow out the candles on a birthday cake. Which of the following sets of muscle activities is primarily responsible for this forceful expiration?
options: Contraction of internal intercostal muscles and abdominal muscles
Relaxation of diaphragm and abdominal muscles
Contraction of diaphragm and external intercostal muscles
questions.solution:
Normal expiration is a passive process that occurs due to the relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles, returning the thoracic cavity to its original volume.

However, forceful expiration is an active process. According to NCERT, we have the ability to increase the strength of expiration with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen. Along with abdominal muscles, the contraction of internal intercostal muscles further pulls the ribs downward and inward. This actively decreases the volume of the thoracic cavity beyond the normal resting state, increasing the intrapulmonary pressure significantly above atmospheric pressure to forcefully expel air.

Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals (option 4) causes inspiration, not expiration.

Answer: Contraction of internal intercostal muscles and abdominal muscles

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the tissues, the oxygen dissociation curve shifts to the right, promoting the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

Reason (R): High $pCO_2$, high $H^+$ concentration, and higher temperature in the tissues decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The oxygen dissociation curve represents the percentage saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen at different partial pressures of oxygen ($pO_2$).

In the tissues, metabolic activities consume oxygen and produce carbon dioxide, leading to low $pO_2$ and high $pCO_2$. The high $pCO_2$ leads to an increase in $H^+$ concentration (lower pH). Additionally, the temperature in active tissues is slightly higher.

According to NCERT, these conditions (high $pCO_2$, high $H^+$ concentration, and higher temperature) decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen. This decreased affinity is graphically represented as a shift of the oxygen dissociation curve to the right, which favours the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains why the curve shifts to the right in the tissues.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced expiration.
Reason (R) : Vital capacity includes Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), Tidal Volume (TV), and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because Vital Capacity (VC) is defined as the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration, or the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration. It is physically impossible to breathe out further immediately after a forced expiration.

Reason (R) is true because Vital Capacity is indeed the sum of Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), Tidal Volume (TV), and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV).

Therefore, the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following groups of animals exchange O_2$ with CO_2$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms exchange O_2$ with CO_2$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.

Earthworms use their moist cuticle for gas exchange.

Insects have a network of tracheal tubes to transport atmospheric air within the body.

Aquatic arthropods use special vascularised structures called gills.

Answer: Sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A graph of the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve shows a standard sigmoid curve (Curve A) and a second curve (Curve B) which is shifted to the right relative to Curve A. Which of the following sets of physiological conditions in the blood would cause the shift from Curve A to Curve B?
options: Low pC$O_2$, high pH, and low temperature
High pC$O_2$, low H$^+$ concentration, and low temperature
High pC$O_2$, high H$^+$ concentration, and higher temperature
High pO_2$, high pCO_2$, and high pH
questions.solution:
A rightward shift in the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve indicates a decrease in the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, which facilitates the unloading of oxygen.

According to NCERT, the conditions that favour dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin (a right shift) are low pO_2$, high pCO_2$, high H$^+$ concentration (which means low pH), and higher temperature.

These conditions are typically found in the systemic tissues. Low pCO_2$, high pH (low H$^+$), and low temperature would cause a left shift (increased affinity), which occurs in the alveoli. \\ \\ Answer: High pCO_2$, high H$^+$ concentration, and higher temperature

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Under normal physiological conditions, every $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood delivers around $20\text{ ml}$ of $\text{O}_2$ to the tissues.

Reason (R): In the tissues, low $\text{pO}_2$, high $\text{pCO}_2$, high $\text{H}^+$ concentration and higher temperature exist, which are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because under normal physiological conditions, every $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood can deliver around $5\text{ ml}$ of $\text{O}_2$ to the tissues, not $20\text{ ml}$. While $100\text{ ml}$ of oxygenated blood carries about $20\text{ ml}$ of $\text{O}_2$, it only unloads approximately $25\%$ (i.e., $5\text{ ml}$) to the tissues under resting conditions.

Reason (R) is true. In the tissues, conditions such as low $\text{pO}_2$, high $\text{pCO}_2$, high $\text{H}^+$ concentration, and higher temperature shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the right. These factors are favourable for the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin, facilitating its delivery to the tissues.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following anatomical sequences represents the part of the human respiratory system responsible for clearing inhaled air from foreign particles, humidifying it, and bringing it to body temperature?
options: External nostrils up to respiratory bronchioles
External nostrils up to terminal bronchioles
External nostrils up to initial bronchioles
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitutes the conducting part of the respiratory system.

The conducting part transports atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies it, and brings the inhaled air to body temperature.

The respiratory bronchioles and alveoli form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system, not the conducting part. The incomplete cartilaginous rings extend only up to the initial bronchioles, but the conducting part extends further up to the terminal bronchioles.

Answer: External nostrils up to terminal bronchioles

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The diffusion of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ from tissues into the systemic blood is independent of the cellular utilisation of $\mathrm{O}_2$.
Reason (R): Catabolic reactions in the cells continuously consume $\mathrm{O}_2$ and release $\mathrm{CO}_2$, creating a partial pressure gradient between tissues and systemic capillaries.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is not correct because the diffusion of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ from tissues into the blood is directly driven by the cellular utilisation of $\mathrm{O}_2$.

Reason (R) is correct. During cellular respiration, catabolic reactions continuously consume $\mathrm{O}_2$ and release $\mathrm{CO}_2$. This metabolic activity increases the partial pressure of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ ($p\mathrm{CO}_2$) in the tissues compared to the systemic capillaries, creating the concentration gradient necessary for the passive diffusion of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ into the blood.

Thus, Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.

Answer: Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Consider the following reversible reaction involved in the transport of respiratory gases:

$\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{HCO}_3^- + \text{H}^+$

Which specific condition at the alveolar site drives this reaction to the left (towards the formation of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$), and what is the relative concentration of the enzyme catalyzing this reaction in the blood plasma?
options: High $p\text{O}_2$ drives the reaction; the enzyme is present in high concentration in plasma
Low $p\text{CO}_2$ drives the reaction; the enzyme is present in high concentration in plasma
Low $p\text{CO}_2$ drives the reaction; the enzyme is present in minute quantities in plasma
High $p\text{CO}_2$ drives the reaction; the enzyme is present in minute quantities in plasma
questions.solution:
The reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme carbonic anhydrase.

According to NCERT, RBCs contain a very high concentration of carbonic anhydrase, while only minute quantities of the same are present in the blood plasma.

At the tissue site, high $p\text{CO}_2$ drives the reaction to the right (forming bicarbonate and hydrogen ions). However, at the alveolar site where $p\text{CO}_2$ is low, the reaction proceeds in the opposite direction (to the left), leading to the formation of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ so that carbon dioxide can be exhaled.

Thus, low $p\text{CO}_2$ is the driving condition, and the enzyme is present in minute quantities in the plasma.

Answer: Low $p\text{CO}_2$ drives the reaction; the enzyme is present in minute quantities in plasma

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding respiration in frogs:

I. In water, skin acts as the aquatic respiratory organ.
II. Gas exchange through the skin occurs by active transport of dissolved oxygen.
III. On land, the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs act as respiratory organs.
IV. The lungs of a frog are paired, elongated, pinkish, sac-like structures present in the upper part of the trunk region.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: In water, frogs exhibit cutaneous respiration where the moist skin acts as the sole respiratory organ.

Statement II is incorrect: Gas exchange through the skin occurs by simple diffusion, not by active transport.

Statement III is correct: On land, frogs use three distinct organs for respiration: the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs.

Statement IV is correct: According to NCERT, the lungs of a frog are a pair of elongated, pinkish, sac-like structures located in the upper part of the trunk region (thorax).

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the tissues, carbon dioxide diffuses into red blood cells (RBCs) and reacts with water in the presence of the enzyme carbonic anhydrase to form carbonic acid, which then dissociates into bicarbonate and hydrogen ions ($H^+$). How does the generation of these $H^+$ ions directly assist in the delivery of oxygen to the tissues?
options: The $H^+$ ions increase the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the left.
The bicarbonate ions bind to the heme group of haemoglobin, physically displacing the bound oxygen molecules.
The $H^+$ ions decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the right.
The consumption of water during the reaction shrinks the RBC, which forces oxygen to diffuse out into the tissues.
questions.solution:
In the tissues, the partial pressure of $CO_2$ is high. $CO_2$ enters the RBCs and undergoes hydration catalyzed by carbonic anhydrase to form $H_2CO_3$, which dissociates into $HCO_3^-$ and $H^+$.

The accumulation of $H^+$ ions increases the $H^+$ concentration (lowers the pH) inside the RBC. A higher $H^+$ concentration decreases the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen. This causes the oxygen dissociation curve to shift to the right, thereby facilitating the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin and its delivery to the tissues.

Option 1 is incorrect because $H^+$ decreases, not increases, oxygen affinity. Option 2 is incorrect because bicarbonate does not displace oxygen from the heme group. Option 4 is a fabricated physical mechanism that does not reflect physiological oxygen transport.

Answer: The $H^+$ ions decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the right.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In frogs, dissolved oxygen in water is exchanged through the skin by simple diffusion.
Reason (R): On land, the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs act as the respiratory organs in frogs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
The Assertion (A) is true because in water, frogs rely on cutaneous respiration where dissolved oxygen is exchanged across the highly vascularized moist skin via simple diffusion.

The Reason (R) is also true as adult frogs are amphibious and utilize the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs (pulmonary respiration) for gas exchange when on land.

However, (R) does not explain (A). The mechanism of simple diffusion across the skin is a physical process driven by concentration gradients, which is independent of the anatomical adaptations for terrestrial respiration mentioned in (R).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A healthy adult takes a normal inspiration. Following this, he forcibly exhales as much air as possible. If the total volume of air exhaled by him is $1600$ mL and his tidal volume is $500$ mL, the remaining $1100$ mL of the exhaled air represents his :
questions.solution:
When a person takes a normal inspiration, the volume of air in the lungs increases by the Tidal Volume (TV).

Upon subsequent forced exhalation, the person first exhales the Tidal Volume (to return to the normal resting expiratory level) and then forcibly exhales the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV). The total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration is called the Expiratory Capacity (EC).

Given:
Total exhaled volume (EC) = $1600$ mL
Tidal Volume (TV) = $500$ mL

Since EC = TV + ERV,
$1600$ mL = $500$ mL + ERV
ERV = $1600$ mL - $500$ mL = $1100$ mL.

Thus, the remaining $1100$ mL of the exhaled air represents the Expiratory Reserve Volume. Residual Volume is the air that remains in the lungs and cannot be exhaled, while Vital Capacity and Inspiratory Reserve Volume involve maximal inspiration.

Answer: Expiratory Reserve Volume

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the physiological sequence of human respiration, which of the following events occurs immediately before the utilisation of $\text{O}_2$ by the cells for catabolic reactions?
options: Transport of respiratory gases by the blood
Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ across the alveolar membrane
Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in
questions.solution:
The physiological process of respiration in humans occurs in five sequential steps:
1. Pulmonary ventilation (breathing).
2. Diffusion of gases ($\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$) across the alveolar membrane.
3. Transport of gases by the blood.
4. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues.
5. Utilisation of $\text{O}_2$ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of $\text{CO}_2$ (cellular respiration).

The event that immediately precedes the cellular utilisation of $\text{O}_2$ (step 5) is the diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between the blood and tissues (step 4).

Answer: Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the structures in List-I with their corresponding features or functions in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Conducting part(I) Actual site of diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and atmospheric air
(B) Exchange part(II) Divides at the level of 5th thoracic vertebra
(C) Epiglottis(III) Brings inhaled air to body temperature
(D) Trachea(IV) Prevents the entry of food into the larynx

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The conducting part of the respiratory system (external nostrils to terminal bronchioles) transports atmospheric air, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies it, and brings it to body temperature. Hence, (A) matches with (III).

The exchange part (alveoli and their ducts) is the actual site of diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and atmospheric air. Hence, (B) matches with (I).

The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that prevents the entry of food into the larynx during swallowing. Hence, (C) matches with (IV).

The trachea is a straight tube that divides at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra into right and left primary bronchi. Hence, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the respiratory structures used by frogs at different life stages and in different habitats.

List-IList-II
A. Adult frog in water1. Gills
B. Adult frog on land2. Skin only
C. Tadpole stage3. Buccal cavity, skin, and lungs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Frogs exhibit different modes of respiration depending on their life stage and environment.

In water, adult frogs respire exclusively through their highly vascularised moist skin (cutaneous respiration). Thus, A matches with 2.

On land, adult frogs utilise their buccal cavity, skin, and lungs for gaseous exchange. Thus, B matches with 3.

The larval stage of a frog, known as a tadpole, is fully aquatic and respires using gills, similar to fishes. Thus, C matches with 1.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-2, B-3, C-1.

Answer: A-2, B-3, C-1

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the steps of respiration in humans.

List IList II
A. First stepI. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
B. Second stepII. Transport of gases by the blood
C. Third stepIII. Pulmonary ventilation
D. Fourth stepIV. Diffusion of gases across alveolar membrane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the steps of respiration in humans occur in the following sequence:

First step: Breathing or pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\text{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out (A matches with III).

Second step: Diffusion of gases ($\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$) across the alveolar membrane (B matches with IV).

Third step: Transport of gases by the blood (C matches with II).

Fourth step: Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues (D matches with I).

Fifth step: Utilisation of $\text{O}_2$ by the cells for catabolic reactions (cellular respiration).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Contraction of diaphragm(I) Increases thoracic volume in dorso-ventral axis
(B) Contraction of external intercostal muscles(II) Forceful expiration
(C) Relaxation of diaphragm and external intercostal muscles(III) Increases thoracic volume in antero-posterior axis
(D) Contraction of abdominal muscles(IV) Normal expiration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The mechanism of breathing involves changes in the volume of the thoracic cavity:

Contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis. Hence, (A) matches with (III).

Contraction of the external intercostal muscles lifts up the ribs and sternum, increasing the thoracic volume in the dorso-ventral axis. Hence, (B) matches with (I).

Relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles returns the diaphragm and sternum to their normal positions, reducing thoracic volume and causing normal passive expiration. Hence, (C) matches with (IV).

Humans have the ability to increase the strength of expiration (forceful expiration) with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen. Hence, (D) matches with (II).

The correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : If two men expire the same volume of air after normal inspiration, they have the same expiratory capacity.
Reason : Expiratory capacity includes tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Expiratory capacity (EC) is the total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration. This includes tidal volume and expiratory reserve volume (TV + ERV). Thus, if two men expire the same volume of air after normal inspiration, they have the same expiratory capacity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The ventilation movements of the lungs in mammals are governed by
questions.solution: Ventilation is the movement of air through the conducting passages between the atmosphere and the lungs. The air moves through the passage because of pressure gradients that are produced by contraction and relaxation of diaphragm and intercostal muscles during inspiration and expiration.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Assertion : The dorsal respiratory group (DRG) present in the dorsal portion of medulla oblongata mainly causes expiration. Reason : The ventral respiratory group (VRG) on the ventrolateral part of medulla oblongata mainly controls inspiration.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Dorsal respiratory group is a type of group located in dorsal portion of the medulla oblongata which mainly causes inspiration. Ventral respiratory group is located in the ventrolateral part of the medulla oblongata which can cause either inspiration or expiration depending upon the neurons stimulated.

options: forceful contraction of intercostal muscles during deep breathing
vibration of the soft palate during breathing while sleeping

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Carbon dioxide $\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right)$ diffuses into blood from tissue site and passes to alveolar site in the form of
questions.solution: Blood is the medium of transport of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Nearly $20-25 \%$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is transported by RBCs as carbaminohaemoglobin whereas $70 \%$ of it is carried as bicarbonate through plasma. About $7 \%$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is carried in dissolved state through plasma. The largest fraction of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is converted to bicarbonate ions $\left(\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}\right)$and transported in plasma. When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ diffuses into the RBCs, it combines with $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$, forming carbonic acid $\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3\right) . \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ is unstable and quickly dissociates into hydrogen ions and bicarbonate ions.

questions.solution: Bohr's effect is the phenomenon whereby the affinity of the respiratory pigment i.e., haemoglobin in the blood for oxygen is reduced when the level of carbon dioxide is increased. An increase in carbon dioxide concentration makes the blood more acidic which results in decrease in the efficiency of the uptake of oxygen by haemoglobin molecules. This facilitates gaseous exchange, because more oxygen is released in the tissues where the amount of carbon dioxide is rising due to metabolic activity. In its reverse, more oxygen is taken up at the lungs where the amount of carbon dioxide is low.

questions.solution: During strenuous exercise, the muscle does not get sufficient oxygen to meet its energy needs immediately. So, it contracts anaerobically and accumulates lactic acid. During recovery, the oxygen consumption of the muscle far exceeds than that in the resting state. The extra oxygen consumed during recovery is called oxygen debt of the muscle.

questions.solution: Human beings have a significant ability to maintain and moderate the respiratory rhythm to suit the demands of the body tissues. A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation. A chemosensitive area is situated adjacent to the rhythm centre which is highly sensitive to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and hydrogen ions. Increase in these substances can activate this centre, which in turn can signal the rhythm centre to make necessary adjustments in the respiratory process.

questions.solution: The word "emphysema" means "inflation" or "full of air". Emphysema is an inflation or abnormal distension of the bronchioles or alveolar sacs of the lungs. It causes irreversible distension and loss of elasticity of alveoli. As a result, the alveolar sacs remain filled with air even after expiration. The exhalation becomes more difficult. The lungs remain inflated. Many of the septa between the alveoli are destroyed and much of the elastic tissue of the lungs is replaced by connective tissue. Major causes are cigarette smoking and the inhalation of other smoke or toxic substances over a period of time.

questions.solution: Trachea and large bronchi are lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium bearing glandular cells (mucous gland). The secretion of mucous glands keeps the walls of trachea and large bronchi moist and traps dust particles which enter with the air. The vibratile cilia of the epithelium then carry the mucous containing dust particles upto the larynx where they can be spitted out.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following match is correct?
options: Emphysema : reduction of surface area of alveoli and bronchi
Asthma : excessive secretion of bronchial mucus
questions.solution: Emphysema means abnormal accumulation of air in the tissues (lungs). In pulmonary emphysema the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs are enlarged and damaged, which reduces the surface area for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. Severe emphysema causes breath-lessness, which is made worse by infections. Pneumonia is inflammation of the lung caused by bacteria, in which the air sacs (alveoli) become filled with inflammatory cells and the lung becomes solid. The symptoms include those of any infection (fever, malaise, headaches, etc.), together with cough and chest pain. Silicosis, a lung disease, is a form of pneumoconiosis produced by inhaling silica dust particles. It affects workers in hard-rock mining and tunnelling, quarrying, stone dressing, sand blasting, and boiler scaling. Silica stimulates fibrosis of lung tissue, which produces progressive breathlessness and considerebly increased susceptibility to tuberculosis. Asthma is the condition of subjects with widespread narrowing of the bronchial airways, which changes in severity over short periods of time (either spontaneously or under treatment) and leads to cough, wheezing, and difficulty in breathing.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The respiratory centre in the brain is stimulated by
questions.solution: Respiratory centre controls the rate of respiration. Respiratory centre is located in medulla oblongata and pons. It has the following components (i) inspiratory area - connected to inspiratory muscles, (ii) Pneum otaxic area, (iii) Expiratory area, (iv) chemosensitive area. Chemoreceptors located on carotid and aortic bodies are sensitive to carbon dioxide levels in arterial blood. They send information to respiratory centre. Oxygen does not have a significant direct effect on the respiratory centre of the brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During chloride shift or Hamburger phenomenon, when the whole blood is saturated with $\mathrm{CO}_2$, following changes occurs. Which one of them is not correct?
options: Bicarbonate content of plasma and corpuscles increase
Chloride content of plasma diminished and that of the cell is increased
Total base of blood remain unchanged
Water content and volume of corpuscles decrease
questions.solution:
According to Hamburger phenomenon, when the whole blood is saturated with carbon dioxide, the following changes are seen
(i) The bicarbonate contents of plasma and corpuscles increase.
(ii) The chloride content of plasma is diminished and that of the cell is increased.
(iii) The total base (cations) of both plasma and corpuscles remain unchanged.
(iv) The water content and the volume of corpuscles increase.
(v) When the carbon dioxide is removed from the blood reverse changes takes place.
(vi) When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ enters blood, $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$from plasma enters RBCs leaving $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$behind. When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ escapes from blood. $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$leaves the cell and combines with $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$again. Due to this alternate movement of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions, this phenomenon is called chloride shift.

questions.solution:
The vital capacity is the maximum amount of air that can be expelled from lungs by forced exhalation after a forced inhalation. It is equal to the sum of tidal volume (TV), inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) and expiratory reserve volume (ERV).
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{VC} & =\mathrm{TV}+\mathrm{IRV}+\mathrm{ERV} \\ & =500+3000+1100 \\ & =4600 \mathrm{ml}\end{aligned}$
